{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |year = 2018–19 |team = Kansas Jayhawks |sport = Basketball |image = University of Kansas athletics (logo).svg |image_size = 150px |conference = Big 12 Conference |division = |short_conf = Big 12 |CoachRank = 16 |APRank = 17 |record = 26–10 |conf_record = 12–6 |head_coach = [[Bill Self]] |hc_year = 16th |asst_coach1 = [[Jerrance Howard]] |ac1_year = 6th |asst_coach2 = [[Norm Roberts]] |ac2_year = 8th |asst_coach3 = [[Kurtis Townsend]] |ac3_year = 15th |stadium = [[Allen Fieldhouse]] |champion = NIT Season Tip-Off champions |tourney = [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Second Round }} {{2018–19 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2018–19 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kansas]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which was the Jayhawks' 121st basketball season. The Jayhawks, members of the [[Big 12 Conference]], played their home games at [[Allen Fieldhouse]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]]. They were led by 16th year Hall of Fame head coach [[Bill Self]]. ==Season notes== The Jayhawks entered the season with high expectations due to returning All-Big 12 players [[Udoka Azubuike]] and [[LaGerald Vick]], adding three [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 McDonald's All-Americans]], and several transfers coming off their [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] years. Following the 2017–18 season, several sports websites ranked Kansas 1st on their "Way too early rankings" which preview the next season.{{cite web|title=Fresh off Final Four, Kansas leads Way-Too-Early Top 25 for 2018-19|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23653227/kansas-jayhawks-stay-no-1-villanova-wildcats-tumble-post-nba-draft-deadline-top-25|website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|title=Kansas, Duke top way-too-early college basketball rankings for 2018-19|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/college-basketball-top-25-rankings-2018-2019-kentucky-duke-kansas-villanova-nba-draft/699qbsghlgh01sfheywp060ox|website=SportingNews.com}}{{cite web|title=2018-19 college basketball rankings: Way-too-early projection has Kansas, Duke at top|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2018-19-college-basketball-rankings-way-too-early-projection-has-kansas-duke-at-top/|website=CBSSports.com}}{{cite web|title=Way-too-early top 25 for the 2018-19 college basketball season|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/way-early-top-25-2018-19-college-basketball-season-033644755.html|website=Sports.Yahoo.com}} The Jayhawks also entered the season ranked number 1 in the AP Poll. Despite the high expectations, the team dealt with adversity during the season as four different players that were expected to be starters missed time. [[Silvio De Sousa]] was declared ineligible by the NCAA,{{cite web |title=Kansas Athletics statements regarding the NCAA decision on Silvio De Sousa |url=https://kuathletics.com/news/2019/2/1/general-kansas-athletics-statement-regarding-the-ncaa-decision-on-silvio-de-sousa.aspx |website=KUAthletics.com}} Udoka Azubuike underwent season ending surgery in January,{{Cite web |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2019/jan/09/doc-says-azubuikes-surgery-couldnt-have-gone-any-b/ |title=Self: Doc says Azubuike’s surgery ‘couldn’t have gone any better’ |last=Tait |first=Matt |date=Jan 9, 2019 |website=KU Sports.com}} Marcus Garrett missed five games due to injury,{{cite web |title=Bill Self updates timetable for Marcus Garrett's return |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/KU-basketball-injury-update-on-Marcus-Garrett-from-Bill-Self-128887897/ |website=247Sports.com}} and [[LaGerald Vick]] took a leave absence in February to handle personal issues and eventually announced he wouldn't return.{{cite web |title=Vick to take leave of absence from Kansas basketball team |url=https://kuathletics.com/news/2019/2/7/mens-basketball-vick-to-take-leave-of-absence-from-kansas-basketball-team.aspx |website=KUAthletics.com}} On February 23, 2019, the Jayhawks lost to Texas Tech 91–62. The loss was the Jayhawks worst conference loss under Bill Self and worst conference loss since the [[1999–2000 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|1999–2000 season]] when they lost to Oklahoma State 86–53.
